## Intent reconstruction

**What it does:** Extracts the "mark as complete" footer bar + note-dialog + `updateServiceRequest` mutation out of [`ServiceRequestShow.tsx`](src/pages/Facility/services/serviceRequests/ServiceRequestShow.tsx) into a new [`CompleteServiceRequestDialog`](src/pages/Facility/services/serviceRequests/components/CompleteServiceRequestDialog.tsx), and extracts the mobile-`Sheet`/desktop-`Dialog` branch into a reusable [`ResponsiveDialog`](src/components/ui/responsive-dialog.tsx) primitive.

**Why:** The prior state of this PR had moved the mutation into `CompletionNoteContent` (to dedupe the two identical `useMutation` calls) but left the *open state* in the parent, so `onOpenChange={setIsCompleteDialogOpen}` lost the `isPending` guard that used to block closing mid-request (`if (!isCompletingServiceRequest) setIsCompleteDialogOpen(open)`). Reuniting state + mutation + dialog in one component (with `handleOpenChange`) restores that guard for every close vector (X button, Escape, overlay click, cancel) — this is the correct fix for the described bug.

**Confidence:** high — verified against the `origin/develop...HEAD` + working-tree diff.

## Findings

**Broken — note draft isn't reset when the dialog reopens**
`CompleteServiceRequestDialog` seeds `note` once via `useState(serviceRequest.note ?? "")` at mount, and never re-syncs it. The pre-refactor code explicitly reset the draft on the trigger's `onClick` (`setCompletionNote(request.note ?? "")` before opening) — that reset is gone. Concretely: type a note → Cancel → reopen → the unsaved draft is still there instead of being discarded (and if this component ever persists across a different `serviceRequestId`, e.g. navigated without remount, it'll show the wrong request's stale note). Minimal fix — restore the reset in the trigger handler:
```tsx
onClick={() => {
  setNote(serviceRequest.note ?? "");
  setIsOpen(true);
}}
```

**Broken (verify in browser) — `contentClassName` conflates Dialog and Sheet sizing**
[`responsive-dialog.tsx`](src/components/ui/responsive-dialog.tsx) forwards the same `contentClassName` to both variants. The caller passes `contentClassName="sm:max-w-lg"`. `DialogContent` is `top-50%/left-50%` + `translate` so a max-width there is safely centered — but `SheetContent side="bottom"` is `inset-x-0` with no `mx-auto`. Pinning both `left` and `right` while also capping `max-width` is an over-constrained box (browser drops `right`, left-aligns), so on viewports where the Sheet is still active (`isMobile` is true up to `lg`, i.e. ≤1023px) the bottom sheet could render capped and left-aligned instead of full-bleed. Worth a quick check at ~700–900px width; if confirmed, either don't forward `contentClassName` to `SheetContent`, or use a separate `sheetClassName`/`dialogClassName` prop.

**Polish — trigger button lost its pending guard**
The old "Mark as complete" button had `disabled={isCompletingServiceRequest}`. In the new component it's unconditional. Harmless in practice (the open dialog's `z-50` overlay sits above the `z-40` footer bar so it can't be clicked anyway), but cheap to restore for parity: `disabled={isCompletingServiceRequest}`.

## Approach (Lens 2)

Reasonable and proportionate. I checked for an existing shared wrapper before flagging this as premature abstraction — there isn't one; the mobile-`Sheet`/desktop-`Dialog` (or Popover/Drawer) branch is duplicated ad hoc in ~10+ places (`RequirementsSelector.tsx`, `AssociateDeviceSheet.tsx`, `AddChargeItemsBillingSheet.tsx`, `AddMultipleChargeItemsSheet.tsx`, etc.). Placing `ResponsiveDialog` in `src/components/ui/` with a single current caller is fine since that's the intended shared-primitives location, and the extraction directly serves the stated goal (mutation + dialog ownership must live together for the `isPending` guard to work). No unused flags or speculative generality.

## Legibility (Lens 1)

Names are self-explanatory (`ResponsiveDialog`, `CompleteServiceRequestDialog`, `handleOpenChange`), and the one comment (`// Keep the dialog open while the completion request is in flight.`) states the non-obvious "why" rather than restating the code. No further legibility gaps.
